title: Horizontal Multistage Pump

introduction.definition: A horizontal multistage pump places several impellers in series on one shaft, so each stage adds roughly the same head and pressure builds up stage by stage. After every impeller a diffuser converts velocity into pressure and return vanes lead the liquid to the next impeller eye. The axial thrust of the impellers is balanced by a balance drum, balance disc or opposed impellers, with a thrust bearing for the residual.
applications: Reverse-osmosis (RO) feed and high-pressure membrane systems
High-rise building water supply and pressure boosting
key_points: Head ≈ number of stages × head per stage
Ring-section (BB4) stages clamped by tie bolts; barrel (BB5) for the highest pressures
First stage sets the NPSH required

classification.configuration: Horizontal, between bearings, radially split ring-section (segmental)
classification.api_610_type: BB4 (single casing, radially split, multistage); barrel BB5 and axially split BB3 are alternatives

introduction.summary: A horizontal multistage pump places several impellers in series on one shaft. Each stage — impeller, diffuser and return channel — adds roughly the same head, so the pressure builds up stage by stage from suction to discharge. The impeller flings liquid outward and raises its velocity and pressure; the diffuser vanes slow it down and convert velocity into more pressure; the return vanes guide it back inward, without swirl, to the eye of the next impeller. Because every impeller faces the same way, their axial thrusts add up; a balance drum at the discharge end, with a leak-off line back to suction, cancels most of it, and a thrust bearing takes the rest. Multistage pumps serve high-head duties such as boiler feed, reverse-osmosis feed, high-rise water supply, mine dewatering and pressure boosting.

what_to_look_for: Liquid enters the suction casing at the lowest pressure in the pump.
The first-stage impeller raises velocity and pressure; this stage sets the pump's NPSH requirement.
The diffuser vanes around the impeller slow the liquid and convert velocity into pressure.

steps.text: Liquid enters the suction casing at the lowest pressure in the pump.
The first-stage impeller raises velocity and pressure; this stage sets the pump's NPSH requirement.
The diffuser vanes around the impeller slow the liquid and convert velocity into pressure.
Return vanes guide the liquid inward, without swirl, to the eye of the next impeller.
Each further stage adds about the same head, so the pressure rises in equal steps towards discharge.
All impellers face the same way, so their axial thrusts add towards suction.
The balance drum has discharge pressure on one side and near-suction pressure on the other; this opposes the impeller thrust.
Leakage past the drum returns to suction through the leak-off line; its flow is a useful wear indicator.
Tie bolts clamp the stage stack between the suction and discharge casings.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Steep head–flow curve (head is the sum of the stage heads); efficiency peak at BEP; power rises with flow; NPSHr set by the first stage.

pressure.title: Stage-by-stage pressure
pressure.description: Colour rings show static pressure rising from suction (blue) to discharge (red). Each stage adds roughly the same head, so total head ≈ number of stages × head per stage at the same flow.

thrust.title: Axial thrust & balancing
thrust.description: Each impeller is pushed towards suction (magenta) because its back shroud sees higher pressure than the eye side. The balance drum (green) has full discharge pressure on its inner face and near-suction pressure in the balance chamber behind it (leak-off line), creating an opposing force. A thrust bearing carries the small residual.

foundation: Rigid grouted baseplate; check that both bearing housings are fully supported.
alignment: Align pump and motor shafts with dial indicators or laser after grouting and again after connecting the piping (hot alignment check for hot service).
Target the coupling manufacturer's tolerances; typical practice for 1500–3000 rpm is ≤0.05 mm offset and ≤0.05 mm/100 mm angularity — verify.
Correct soft foot (< 0.05 mm) before final alignment.
Check axial float/rotor position after coupling up.
piping: Support suction and discharge piping independently so nozzle loads stay within the manufacturer's (or API 610/HI 9.6.2) allowable values.
Provide a straight run of at least 5 pipe diameters ahead of the suction nozzle (ANSI/HI 9.6.6 guidance — verify) and use an eccentric reducer with the flat side up.
Fit isolation valves on both sides, a check valve on the discharge, and pressure gauges at suction and discharge.
Never use the pump as a pipe anchor; use expansion joints with tie rods only when designed for them.
Route the balance leak-off line back to suction without valves that could be closed.
Install a minimum-flow recirculation line where low-flow operation is possible.
commissioning: Fill and vent the casing; never run dry.
Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Start against a partly open discharge valve, then open to the duty point; avoid running at shut-off.
Record baseline vibration, bearing temperature, suction and discharge pressure, flow and motor current.
Warm up hot-service pumps uniformly before starting.
Never start with the discharge and minimum-flow lines both closed.

routine.task: Check balance leak-off flow/temperature against the baseline.
Check seal leakage at both ends.

periodic.task: Check tie-bolt tension per the manual after thermal cycles.

overhaul.task: Dismantle the stage stack; measure impeller, diffuser and balance-drum clearances.
Inspect the first-stage impeller for cavitation damage.

lubrication: Oil-lubricated bearings (ring oil or forced feed on large units).

causes: Running at low flow / thermal distortion
Insufficient NPSHa (hot water, low deaerator level)
Worn interstage bushes and wear rings

video_tutorials.title: Horizontal Multistage Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Horizontal Multistage Pump.
Monitor thrust-bearing temperature.
Check balance leak-off flow/temperature against the baseline.
Check seal leakage at both ends.
Check tie-bolt tension per the manual after thermal cycles.
Change bearing oil.
Dismantle the stage stack; measure impeller, diffuser and balance-drum clearances.
Inspect the first-stage impeller for cavitation damage.
Watch for balance drum wear: rising leak-off flow. Common cause: abrasives.
Watch for first-stage cavitation: noise. Common cause: insufficient NPSHa (hot water, low deaerator level).
Watch for overheating at low flow: rising casing temperature. Common cause: operation below minimum flow.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: A pump has 6 identical stages each producing 40 m at the duty flow. What is the approximate total head?
questions.explanation: Heads of stages in series add: 6 × 40 m = 240 m (ignoring small internal losses).

questions.question: What is the job of the return vanes?
options: Guide liquid from the diffuser back to the next impeller eye without swirl
questions.explanation: They turn the flow inward and remove swirl so the next impeller receives a clean inlet flow.

questions.question: Why do the axial thrusts of the impellers add up in this pump?
options: All impellers face the same direction (inline arrangement)
questions.explanation: Each impeller is pushed towards its suction side.

questions.question: What keeps the balance chamber behind the drum near suction pressure?
options: The leak-off line back to suction
questions.explanation: Without the leak-off the chamber would rise to discharge pressure and the drum would not balance anything.

questions.question: Rising balance leak-off flow usually indicates…
Which stage determines the NPSH required of the whole pump?
questions.explanation: Only the first stage sees suction pressure.

questions.question: Why is a minimum-flow line important on a multistage pump?
options: To prevent overheating and instability at very low flow
questions.explanation: At low flow most input power heats the liquid inside the pump.

questions.question: Which API 610 type is a radially split, multistage barrel pump?
questions.explanation: BB5 is the double-casing barrel design; BB4 is single-casing ring-section.
